page: Microsoft Azure D96ls_v6 is a compute-focused virtual machine from the Dlsv6 server family, running on the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor. It features 96 dedicated vCPUs mapped to 48 physical cores of an Intel Xeon 8573C processor operating at 4.2 GHz. The x86_64 architecture includes a 260 MB L3 cache and advanced instruction sets, notably Intel Advanced Matrix Extensions (AMX_TILE, AMX_INT8) and Advanced Vector Extensions (AVX-512). The system is configured with 192.0 GB of system memory, yielding a resource density of 2.0 GB of RAM per vCPU. It does not include local storage or onboard GPUs, though it is Premium Storage capable for remote disk attachments.

Benchmark evaluations demonstrate strong multi-core capabilities and high-throughput processing. The server achieves top-tier status in Passmark CPU scores (86,191.93) and Geekbench multi-core performance (21,482.0). Its multi-threaded bzip3 decompression reaches 509.95 GB/sec, and static web serving throughput is highly efficient at 115.45 GB/sec. Memory bandwidth is robust, with cached small-block reads at 6,201.65 GB/sec and uncached large-block reads at 257.01 GB/sec. Single-core performance, such as stress-ng single-core and single-threaded gzip compression, sits in the average tier, indicating that workloads must be highly parallelized to fully exploit the hardware.

Given its high vCPU count relative to memory capacity, the D96ls_v6 offers a cost-efficient profile for compute-heavy workloads that do not require massive memory footprints. The inclusion of Intel AMX and AVX-512 instructions makes it highly suitable for CPU-based machine learning tasks, as evidenced by strong prompt processing speeds in LLM inference benchmarks. It is well-suited for parallel processing tasks, software compilation, image processing, and high-throughput web serving, whereas memory-bound databases or large-scale in-memory caching may find the 2.0 GB per core allocation restrictive.
